theme: Late-summer dispensa — fresh borlotti beans + tomato confit as the week's two building blocks (2 adults, technique week)

components.name: Fresh borlotti (cranberry) bean conserva
components.ingredients: 2 lb fresh borlotti/cranberry beans in pod (or 1 lb dried cannellini soaked), soffritto (onion, carrot, celery), 4 garlic cloves, Parmesan rind, 3 anchovies, sage, bay, small piece kombu, olive oil
components.method: Shell the fresh beans. Sweat a fine soffritto in a generous pour of olive oil until sweet, melt in the anchovies, add garlic and sage. Add beans, Parmesan rind, bay, kombu, and water to cover by two fingers. Barely simmer 45–60 min until creamy but intact (dried cannellini ~75–90 min). Season at the end; keep them brothy — that pot liquor is a sauce. Cool in the liquid; refrigerate up to 5 days.

components.name: Cherry tomato & garlic confit
components.ingredients: 3 pints cherry/grape tomatoes, 1 head garlic (cloves peeled), rosemary + thyme sprigs, chili flakes, 2–3 cups olive oil, flaky salt
components.method: Nestle tomatoes and whole garlic cloves in a small baking dish with herbs and chili, cover completely with olive oil. Confit at 300°F for ~50 min until the tomatoes slump and burst and the garlic is jammy. Cool in the oil. You now have sweet tomatoes, soft garlic, and a spectacular infused oil — all three get used all week. Keeps 1 week submerged.

dinners.name: Spaghetti al pomodoro confit
dinners.ingredients: Spaghetti, tomato confit + its oil, confit garlic, basil, Parmesan
steps: Boil spaghetti in well-salted water; reserve a mug of pasta water.
Warm a big spoonful of confit tomatoes, smashed confit garlic, and a few tbsp of the tomato oil in a wide pan.
Drag in the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water; toss hard to emulsify into a glossy sauce.
Off heat, add torn basil and grated Parmesan; finish with more tomato oil.

dinners.name: Olive-oil-poached cod over brothy borlotti
dinners.ingredients: 2 cod or halibut fillets, tomato confit oil, borlotti beans + their broth, lemon, parsley
steps: Warm the beans in their broth with a ladle of confit tomatoes; keep at a bare simmer.
Submerge cod fillets in warm confit oil (about 130–140°F) in a small pan; poach gently 10–12 min until just flaking.
Spoon brothy beans into bowls; lift the fish on top.
Finish with lemon, parsley, flaky salt, and a spoon of the poaching oil.

dinners.name: Clams with borlotti in tomato-confit brodo
dinners.ingredients: 1.5 lb littleneck clams, borlotti beans + broth, tomato confit, white wine, confit garlic, crusty bread
steps: Sizzle smashed confit garlic and confit tomatoes in a little tomato oil in a deep pan.
Add a splash of white wine and the bean broth; bring to a simmer.
Add clams, cover, and steam 4–6 min until they open (discard any that don't).
Stir in the beans to warm through; serve in bowls with grilled bread rubbed in confit oil.

dinners.name: Chard & borlotti with a fried egg
dinners.ingredients: 2 bunches Swiss chard, borlotti beans + broth, confit garlic, eggs, Parmesan, chili flakes
steps: Wilt chopped chard in confit oil with smashed confit garlic and chili flakes.
Add the beans with a little broth; simmer until saucy and glossy.
Fry eggs in confit oil until edges are crisp, yolks runny.
Plate the beans and greens, set an egg on each, shower with Parmesan and a drizzle of oil.

technique.name: Olive-oil confit / low-temperature oil poaching
technique.tiedTo: The cherry tomato & garlic confit, then carried into the poached-cod dinner. The skill is holding the oil low and steady (300°F in the oven for the tomatoes; ~130–140°F on the stove for the fish) so ingredients cook through gently without frying — silky texture and a reusable infused oil as the payoff.

shopping.items: 2 lb fresh borlotti/cranberry beans in pod, 3 pints cherry/grape tomatoes, 2 bunches Swiss chard, 2 heads garlic, 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stalk, basil, parsley, lemons, rosemary, thyme, sage
2 cod or halibut fillets (~3/4 lb), 1.5 lb littleneck clams
Spaghetti, anchovies, kombu, chili flakes, bay leaves, crusty bread, dry white wine, large bottle good olive oil (you'll go through 3–4 cups this week)

scaleNote: This is a 2-adult week (girls with Jen Sep 8–21), so quantities above serve Dan + Mike. For a full-house week (6, four girls under 10): double both components — 4 lb beans, 6 pints tomatoes, ~5–6 cups oil. Lean on the kid-friendly dishes: double the spaghetti al pomodoro (kids love the sweet confit tomatoes), and turn the chard-and-egg into a bigger skillet with eggs cooked to each kid's liking. For the fish night, poach a larger cod fillet and flake it into the beans so it's forkable and mild; serve clams mainly for the adults with plenty of bread for dunking.
